newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGC WINS 20 BLN YEN PHILIPPINE POLYETHYLENE ORDER.
newsitem.headline: JGC WINS 20 BLN YEN PHILIPPINE POLYETHYLENE ORDER.

text.p: JGC Corp said on Wednesday it had won a 20 billion yen order from Bataan Polyethylene Corp (BPC) to build a polyethylene plant in the Philippines.

Under the terms of the contract, the engineering firm is to build the plant, with an annual output capacity of 200,000 tonnes, by the end of 1999 in Limay on the Bataan Peninsula, a company spokesman said.

BPC is owned 45 percent by Bataan Polyethylene Holdings Corp, 30 percent by British Petroleum Co Plc subsidiary BP Holdings International BV, and 20 percent by Malaysia's state-run oil firm Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), he said.
The remaining five percent is held by Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp.
Demand for polyethylene, which is used to manufacture products such as
grocery bags, trash bags and agricultural covers, is increasing sharply in the Philippines as the country's economy grows, the spokesman said.
